podcast.title: Model for Future PBS Specials
podcast.body: The unexpected and massive success of The Three Tenors' concert during the PBS Pledge Drive in 1991 served as a critical blueprint and inspiration for other artists, most notably Yani and John Tesh, who observed this phenomenon and recognized the potential of public television as a "catapult" for their careers. "Yani and his producer, George Varis, they saw what was happening. They saw the PBS Pledge Drive as a platform."

podcast.title: Pledge Drive Success and Mainstream Impact
podcast.body: The concert's airing during the March 1991 PBS Pledge Drive was an unprecedented fundraising success, generating "tonnemae" for PBS and causing the popularity of the three tenors to "spill over and spilled out... into the mainstream," making them household names. This demonstrated the immense power of PBS pledge drives to launch artists into broader recognition. "We made tonnemae. We made a tonnemae on that. And then it just spilled over and spilled out. Out into the mainstream. The three-tenor's became household names."

podcast.title: Repackaged Concert for PBS
podcast.body: The Three Tenors' concert special was not originally produced for PBS; it had been previously aired by ABC the year before its highly successful run during the March 1991 PBS Pledge Drive. Its repackaging for public television proved to be an unexpected success. "The three-tenor's concert special wasn't made for PBS. ABC had actually aired it the year before."

concerts.title: World Cup in Italy (1990)
concerts.body: The Three Tenors—Jose Carreras, Placido Domingo, and Luciano Pavarotti—performed their first concert together in 1990 as part of the World Cup festivities in Italy. "Jose Carreras, Placido Domingo, and Luciano Pavarotti performed their first concert together in 1990 as part of the World Cup in Italy."

concerts.title: PBS Pledge Drive (March 1991)
concerts.body: The Three Tenors made their "biggest mark" during the March 1991 PBS Pledge Drive, where a repackaged version of their ABC-aired concert special was broadcast. This airing "defied all expectations," generating a significant amount of money for PBS and propelling the tenors into household name status, serving as an inspiration for other artists like Yani and John Tesh. "But the three tenors made their biggest mark during another major week-long event. The March PBS Pledge Drive."
